thread:
frank: Heads-up: noticed a swarm of client errors this morning where apps saw 503 but console flagged them as quota issues. We should decide canonical surface for client-facing codes.

lee: Which region/service?

frank: prod, eu-west, text-generate endpoints. Router applied a soft-throttle policy and returned 503 for transport; SDKs report 503 and show generic retry. Meanwhile console telemetry shows quota-limited.

anya: This mismatch is user-visible and confusing. From product POV the console should show a \"Throughput limited\" badge and the SDK should enable a quota flow (billing CTA) where appropriate.

ben: Ops view: router returns 503 to avoid changing transport semantics during reroutes. But we can add a stable header with the client-intended status and a reason code.

frank: Proposal: keep HTTP 503 for internal routing, but include header `X-Redwood-Client-Info: quota=429;reason=tenant_rate_limit` and add a small JSON body field `client_status: 429`. SDKs should parse header first, then body, then fall back to HTTP status.

maria-ux: For console mapping: if header indicates quota (quota=429) we surface \"Throughput limited\" + link to usage page. If header absent but HTTP 5xx present we show \"Service instability\". Copy should avoid \"internal error\" for quota-limited cases.

lee: Agree. Telemetry needs a single canonical tag. Suggest we emit `route.degrade_reason` with tidy values: \"tenant_quota\", \"node_unavailable\", \"maintenance\". That key drives both dashboards and console badges.

anya: Also important: guidance to clients. For 429 we want them to show a clear billing/upgrade path; but for some soft-degrades we intentionally want clients to back off instead of spamming retries. Need per-policy retryability flag.

ben: Implementation plan: router change adds header and body field. Router also emits `route.degrade_reason` into logs and to metrics. SDKs add precedence parsing and introduce `DegradeError` with metadata {client_status, reason, retryable}.

frank: Example response format we can show in RFC: 
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
X-Redwood-Client-Info: client_status=429;reason=tenant_rate_limit;retryable=false
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "error": "route_degraded",
  "client_status": 429,
  "reason": "tenant_rate_limit",
  "message": "Request routed to degraded mode due to tenant throughput limits"
}
```

lee: Question on backoff: should `retryable=false` be default for quota limits? Product probably wants users to see upgrade UI rather than blind retries.

maria-ux: UX rec: when `client_status==429 && retryable==false` show \"Check usage or request quota increase\" with ability to open support or self-serve limit increase. When true, show suggested retry interval and backoff hint.

anya: Telemetry action: add `route.degrade_reason` to ingestion, and a boolean `client_code_emitted`. We can then run a 48h comparison of old 5xx dashboards vs new degrade dashboards during canary.

ben: Ops-bot: starting canary for header rollout in eu-west at 09:12 UTC.

frank: Also update docs/SDK changelog: new behavior where SDKs prefer `X-Redwood-Client-Info`. Backcompat: if absent, preserve current behavior.

lee: Security note: header might leak tenant state; keep header content non-sensitive and avoid policy details. Only include enum reasons.

anya: I'll draft the RFC with example payloads + SDK guidance + console copy snippets. Maria will provide microcopy. Ben will land the router patch and coordinate canary.

maria-ux: Draft microcopy: \"Throughput limited: Your requests are being throttled to keep latency stable. Visit Usage to adjust limits or contact support.\" Short and action-oriented.

frank: Rollout checklist: RFC merged, router canary, SDK patch (minor), telemetry ingestion update, console badge change, docs + changelog. Recommend a dark-launch period of 72h before wide rollout.

ben: Will add metrics for (route.degrade_reason==\"tenant_quota\") && (client_code_emitted==true) and alert if >3% sustained in 5m.

frank: Thanks all. Please comment on RFC when it's up.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for header rollout in eu-west at 09:12 UTC.

maria-ux: :white_check_mark:
